speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with rectal bleeding and a palpable mass; to determine the cause, I need to ask a few specific questions. First, how old are you, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits like diarrhea or constipation recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rectal Cancer. Given the patient's age (45), the presence of a palpable rectal mass, and a 2-week history of daily painless rectal bleeding, the clinical picture is highly suggestive of malignancy until proven otherwise. I will immediately request a Colonoscopy with biopsy and a CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to confirm the diagnosis and stage the disease.
